Reusable PubMed Search Workflow

Source: vignettes/pubmed-search-workflow.Rmd
pubmed-search-workflow.Rmd

This vignette shows how to use pubmedsearchworkflow to keep PubMed systematic searches reusable across projects. The package separates study-specific search strings from the R code that reads, chunks, runs, combines, and exports PubMed records.

The bundled quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) search is an example study. Use its file layout as a template for new searches rather than editing the package functions.

Install and Load

Install dependencies and this package from a fresh R session opened at the repository root. A fresh session matters on Windows because packages such as cli, fs, and rlang can be locked if they are already loaded by RStudio or another package.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = "never")
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"), c("CMD", "INSTALL", "."))

If installation fails with a message such as cannot remove prior installation or namespace 'fs' ... is being loaded, restart R and run the same commands before loading devtools, pkgdown, or this package.

Load the package:

library(pubmedsearchworkflow)

Locate Example Search Files

When working from the source checkout, paths such as inst/examples/... are available directly. After installation, use system.file() to locate bundled examples inside the installed package.

qac_include <- system.file(
  "examples/qac/search_terms/qac_chemical_string_841.txt",
  package = "pubmedsearchworkflow"
)

qac_exclude <- system.file(
  "examples/qac/search_terms/qac_exclusion_string.txt",
  package = "pubmedsearchworkflow"
)

smoke_query <- system.file(
  "examples/smoke/pubmed_pmid_query.txt",
  package = "pubmedsearchworkflow"
)

file.exists(c(qac_include, qac_exclude, smoke_query))
#> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE

Read and Normalize Queries

Study teams should store PubMed search strings in plain-text files. This makes review, version control, and reuse easier than embedding long Boolean strings in notebooks.

include_query <- read_pubmed_query(smoke_query)
include_query
#> [1] "32678460[PMID]"

read_pubmed_query() collapses line breaks and repeated whitespace so query files can be formatted for readability.

normalize_pubmed_query(c('"alpha"[Title]', " OR ", ' "beta"[Title]'))
#> [1] "\"alpha\"[Title] OR \"beta\"[Title]"

Add Exclusions

Use build_pubmed_query() to combine an include query with optional exclusions. The helper wraps both sides in parentheses to preserve intent.

build_pubmed_query(
  include_query = '"alpha"[Title]',
  exclude_query = '"review"[Publication Type]'
)
#> [1] "(\"alpha\"[Title]) NOT (\"review\"[Publication Type])"

Split Large Top-Level OR Queries

Large chemical-name searches often need to be split into smaller PubMed requests. split_pubmed_or_query() splits only top-level OR operators. It preserves quoted strings and nested parenthetical logic.

example_query <- '("a"[Title] AND ("b"[Title] OR "c"[Title])) OR "d OR e"[Title] OR "f"[Title]'
split_pubmed_or_query(example_query)
#> [1] "(\"a\"[Title] AND (\"b\"[Title] OR \"c\"[Title]))"
#> [2] "\"d OR e\"[Title]"                                
#> [3] "\"f\"[Title]"

For the QAC example, the large include file can be split into chunks before submitting to PubMed.

qac_chunks <- split_pubmed_or_query(read_pubmed_query(qac_include))
length(qac_chunks)
#> [1] 1682
head(qac_chunks, 2)
#> [1] "104-74-5[rn]"                          
#> [2] "\"1-Dodecylpyridinium chloride\"[tiab]"

Run a Live PubMed Search

Live PubMed calls are intentionally not evaluated in this vignette so package checks remain deterministic. Run this smoke test manually when you want to verify local network access and easyPubMed behavior.

results <- run_pubmed_search(
  include_query = read_pubmed_query(smoke_query),
  chunk = FALSE
)

records <- combine_pubmed_data(results)
records[, c("pmid", "title", "year", "jabbrv")]

For a broad query, start with a small chunk limit before launching a full search:

results <- run_pubmed_search(
  include_query = read_pubmed_query(qac_include),
  exclude_query = read_pubmed_query(qac_exclude),
  chunk = TRUE,
  limit = 2,
  sleep = 1
)

records <- combine_pubmed_data(results)

Remove limit = 2 only after the smoke run succeeds.

Export Results

Use write_pubmed_csv() to combine records, deduplicate by PMID, create parent directories, and write a CSV.

write_pubmed_csv(results, "outputs/qac_search_smoke.csv")

Command-Line Runner

Collaborators who do not need to write R code can use the bundled runner from the repository root:

system2(
  "Rscript",
  c(
    "exec/run_pubmed_search.R",
    "--include", "inst/examples/smoke/pubmed_pmid_query.txt",
    "--output", "outputs/smoke_pubmed_pmid.csv",
    "--no-chunk"
  )
)

The runner uses the same package functions as the R API. Use --limit for smoke tests, --sleep to pause between PubMed requests, and --quiet to suppress package-level progress messages.

Recommended Project Pattern

For a new systematic search:

  1. Copy inst/examples/qac/ to a new project-specific folder.
  2. Replace the include and exclusion text files with the new search strategy.
  3. Run a one-PMID or low-limit smoke test.
  4. Commit search-term files and workflow notes.
  5. Keep generated CSV files in outputs/ unless they are final curated deliverables.
